all_words.explanation: A referee is someone who judges the quality of work or performance, just as a reviewer judges a manuscript, so the two words share a core meaning.
A tomato is a vegetable and has no connection to evaluating academic work.
A manuscript is the text that a reviewer reads and assesses, so the two words belong to the same process of academic publishing.
A bucket is a container for liquids and is unrelated to peer review.
'Reviewer feedback' is a common phrase in academic writing, where reviewers give comments to authors.
A hammock is a hanging bed for resting and has no link to academic review.

explanation: The words referee, manuscript and feedback are linked to the idea of a reviewer, while tomato, bucket and hammock are unrelated to it.
